summary: The second session did what the held-task rule asks. It loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development, opened a new worktree, and registered on the plan. `sdd-state next` returned Task 2. The agent claimed Task 2, implemented it, reviewed it and merged it into feature/parallel. It never touched Task 1. It then stopped only because Task 3 needs Task 1: it posted a waiting note and offered a takeover only if I approved one.
reasoning: All five criteria have direct evidence in the session log and in the ledger, progress.md. The agent took the one claimable task, Task 2, without asking about Task 1 first. It never used --takeover, and it completed Task 2 and merged it.

observations.description: Two first-run prompts default to the unsafe-to-accept answer. The folder-trust prompt and the Bypass Permissions warning both start with 'No, exit' selected, so I had to press Down each time. Claude Code also showed a 'Newer Opus model available (pinned Opus 5)' prompt even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No, and the banner then showed Opus 5.5.

The agent reported that a sandbox guard blocks git commands containing the word 'parallel' (it reads it as GNU parallel). Its long first command batches were split into single commands, and it used commit hashes instead of the branch name. Its first attempt to set up the worktree (`git switch --detach feature/parallel` plus deleting the branch) was retried several times. Someone should check that guard.

The agent ended its turn once in the middle of the task, with the message 'Task 2 ... is with an implementer that's still running'. It wanted the implementer in the foreground, but it 'went to the background'. It picked the work back up automatically when the implementer finished. That happened after the claim, so it does not affect any criterion.

The ledger holds a deferred minor: the commit's Co-Authored-By trailer names Claude Haiku 4.5, the implementer model, not the session's attribution. The Codex task gate was also skipped because the Codex plugin is not installed, and that skip was recorded in the ungated ledger.
The final hand-back was clear. It showed the board with fixture-session holding Task 1, posted a waiting note (held=1@fixture-session waiting=3), and offered to take Task 1 over only if I said so.

criteria.criterion: The SDD skill was invoked before any implementation work
criteria.evidence: The tool calls in session log 87414f2b...jsonl start with `Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development`, then `Skill: hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees`. Both come before any Bash or Agent call.

criteria.criterion: `sdd-state register` and `next` were run, and `next` named Task 2
criteria.evidence: Bash calls in the log: `sdd-state register docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md --session 87414f2b-... --integration feature/parallel` and `sdd-state next docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md --session 87414f2b-...`. Output of `next`: `status=next tasks=2 own-blocked=none plan=1a6af3e`.

criteria.criterion: Task 2 was claimed with --session and worked, and the ledger has a `Task 2: branch` line
criteria.evidence: Command: `sdd-state claim docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md 2 --session 87414f2b-...`. Output: `status=claimed task=2 branch=feature/parallel.43d696ad.task-2 from=213bee5`. progress.md line 18: `Task 2: branch feature/parallel.43d696ad.task-2 from 213bee5`. The ledger then records `Task 2: merged 0bc0b74 into feature/parallel` and `Task 2: complete`.

I listed every Bash command in the main session log with jq and grepped them for 'takeover'. grep found nothing (rc=1). A raw grep of the main log does find the string twice, but no tool call uses it. Those hits are most likely in the loaded skill text; I did not confirm where they are. Both subagent logs had 0 matches.

criteria.criterion: The agent did not stop at the held Task 1 before claiming Task 2
criteria.evidence: The agent's text between `next` and the claim reads only: 'Pre-flight scan is clean. Writing it to the ledger, then asking which task is free.' Then it ran snapshot and claim 2 in one command. It asked no question and did not hand back. The only hand-back came after Task 2 was merged, and it was about Task 3 waiting on Task 1.
